Content:
Dan... Let's get one thing straight: You are still true to yourself and your methods and are one of the few YouTubers on the platform who have maintained their style and self that most YouTubers would ditch for the sake of chasing trends.

You do not and that's a blessing. It's no longer about being good at YouTube. It's about being true to yourself. THAT is being actually good at YouTube long-term. That is being good not as some celebrity, but as a human.

Sure, you may count yourself as one of the longest YouTubers on the platforms and the algorithm will make it look bad. But to us who have found you by happy chance, searching or through other ways, algorithms have become irrelevant, redundant and just excessive. You are not a trend. You are a statement.

As such, you are living proof that what is new is not always good - heck, it's become rather bad, mostly. Cherish it just as we as fans who have turned from kids into adults with our own struggles to face cherish it.

Remain true to yourself, Dan. And we must remain true to ourselves.

Author: @CatWithAQuill
Content:
Dan The Diamond Minecart, you are genuinely one of the most admirable people I am aware of. Prioritizing your health and your family over YouTube is a large part of why. I've been watching your channel since I was in fourth grade: I've been watching since custom mod adventures and mod reviews and the old lab, Crazy Craft and The Diamond Dimensions. I'm in college now, and I still click every time I see one of your videos in my recommended. I'm not lying when I say a lot of what you've done is a big part of why I took an interest in art and storytelling to the point that the college major I'm going to complete pretty soon is creative writing. It's what got me into Minecraft, how I've made friends in real life, and how I found half of the communities I love today. You aren't bad at YouTube. YouTube got bad at being a platform that promotes healthy positivity and creativity, but you do and always have done a wonderful job of that.  I'm immensely grateful that you were my introduction to YouTube, and even more so that you're still such an upstanding individual as you are today. 

Long videos and variety are great, but I honestly think the best thing about your channel is how you've found that balance between keeping it alive and staying healthy and happy in your actual life (I haven't forgotten how you were once so dedicated to daily uploads that you still made a video instead of going to the hospital immediately when you injured your wrist [don't remember if it was fractured or broken but jeez]; the fact that now you're taking breaks for hobbies and touching grass and spending time with your family and in general being a healthy human being is literally making me tear up, you are the best example of how this all should work)

Anyway, I'm going to stop being sappy and go watch the deltarune chapter 3 playthrough that the YouTube algorithm has so cruelly hidden from me. Thank you for being amazing <3

Author: @heyimlunac
Content:
Hey dan, your videos get so many views so I'm not sure you're going to be able to read this. I have been watching you for over 10 years, which seems pretty insane since I'm still a teenager but I remember watching your crazy craft videos with Thinknoodles and Diamond Dimensions. It seems a little crazy that we are not kids anymore and some days i think about how time has passed by so fast, some days I sit down and cry (although it sounds a little weird) and just remember how I used to be a kid who wouldn't care about anything; I used to be so stress free in life and wouldn't care about what happens in the future. Now that i'm not longer a kid anymore i remember how your videos raised me, you were the person i started really watching when i was a kid. I feel so caught up with the present that it gives me a sense of relief just watching one of your videos from time to time and just think about the past. 

And i gladly say this, you have raised me, and not just me but an entire generation of people, for those without fathers, for those with depression, for those who were on the risk of suicide, you were the reason we kept living. Every day that we live, we strive to be the person you are, the dad that we didn't have, the friend that we didn't have, the person that we were not. Not a single one of us blame you for taking a break from youtube, we will always be part of your community; whether we are burdened with work or university, or looking for a memory in the past. 

As I tear up writing this,
Thank you Dan
For everything you have done.

Content:
gonna come back and watch this after minecraft live. but, dan, just know that you’ve done your job here! you deserve to take your time and relax!

ok, ive just gotten the chance to watch it. a few comments:

dan, i think the community collectively agrees that it is 110% acceptable that you want to spend time off of content creation and more with your kids/outdoors. honestly, that just makes you a more genuine and likeable youtuber. you've served the entire community of youtube insanely well for the past 10+ years, and how you approach this is entirely your decision. personally, i have no real problem if you only post once every few months, or even feel the need to stop posting altogether. regardless of how you continue with your content, we'll always be here if you choose to return or make larger changes in your lifestyle. 

you wanting to spend more time outside of youtube is very admirable in my opinion. im also chronically indoors, but seeing someone who ive looked up to for so many years make a similar change to something that ive wanted to do just makes you, as i said before, more likeable and relatable. 

side note: for some game suggestions (in case you need a few), i think it would be pretty cool to see a video on deltarune chapter 4, but i think a re-visit to terraria (considering how much it's changed over the years) would be insanely fun for both you and for the audience. also, i totally agreed with your point about playing random indie games. those are some of my favorites to re-visit, they're usually hilariously unexpected, and i think they're also really encouraging for future game developers. essentially, re-visits to old things, along with whatever else you might enjoy!
